data.name: label1.Text
data.value: 1. Egypt is widely recognized as one of the most populous countries in the region, with a rapidly growing population that places increasing pressure on resources and infrastructure. 2. Population density is highly concentrated along the Nile River and within the Nile Delta region, where fertile land, water access, and economic opportunities attract the majority of residents. 3. Over the past few years, the overall population growth rate has shown signs of gradual decline when compared with previous decades, reflecting ongoing demographic and social changes.

data.name: label6.Text
data.value: 1. Egypt is divided into 27 governorates, each with its own unique identity , cultural characteristics, and administrative structure that contribute to the diversity of the nation. 2. Egyptian governorates are commonly classified into Urban, Rural, Border, and Mixed categories according to their geographical location, population distribution, and administrative nature. 3. This classification plays an important role in development planning, especially when estimating essential public services such as education systems, healthcare facilities, and the number of schools required in each governorate. 4. Every governorate is administratively centered around a main capital city, which usually serves as the political, economic, and service hub of the region.
